name: Abū al-Ḥusayn Aḥmad ibn Fāris ibn Zakariyyāʾ al-Rāzī
summary: Lexicographer of Hamadan and Rayy, author of Maqāyīs al-lugha and al-Mujmal, teacher of Badīʿ al-Zamān al-Hamadhānī and of al-Ṣāḥib ibn ʿAbbād; one of the greatest masters of the language in Ibn al-Anbārī's words.
bio: Ibn al-Anbārī calls Ibn Fāris one of the greatest masters of the language. He took from Abū Bakr Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Khaṭīb, the transmitter of Thaʿlab, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm al-Qaṭṭān and from Aḥmad ibn Ṭāhir ibn al-Munajjim, and Badīʿ al-Zamān al-Hamadhānī was among his pupils.
He lived in Hamadan and at the end of his life in Rayy, where he died in 395/1004. His dictionaries, al-Mujmal and Maqāyīs al-lugha, arrange the words by their roots and the root's basic meanings.
uncertain: Ibn al-Anbārī gives no year of death; 395/1004 is the usual date (TDV), others give 390/1000.

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 392–396
